plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Food Webs, Trophic Energy Pyramid, Biomagnification & Keystone Species chart from Charles Elton (1927 Animal Ecology), Raymond Lindeman (October 1942 Ecology 23: 399–417), Rachel Carson (27 September 1962 Silent Spring), and Robert Paine (1966 Am. Nat. 100: 65–75 & 1969 Am. Nat. 103: 91–93) shows 1) Lindeman's ~10% energy transfer per trophic level (~90% lost as metabolic heat); 2) Carson's inverted DDT biomagnification pyramid (0.02 ppm water → 5 ppm plankton → 40–300 ppm fish → 1,600+ ppm grebes/eagles); and 3) Paine's Mukkaw Bay Pisaster removal crashing species diversity from 15 to 8 to 1.

teach_overlay.scale: because ninety percent of all food energy burns away as body heat at every step up the food chain, it takes ten thousand kilograms of grass to feed one thousand kilograms of rabbits, to feed one hundred kilograms of foxes, to keep a single ten-kilogram golden eagle alive
